chapters.title: Introduction
chapters.summary:
Introduction begins with a deliberately chosen anecdote that grounds the argument in lived experience. The scene is detailed with dialogue, location, and artefact, so the reader sees the mechanism before it is named. The chapter reproduces an illustration of the immediate environment — a desk, a prototype, or a screen — photographed or diagrammed with callouts that turn background into evidence. A second chart situates the episode inside a broader distribution, showing where this case sits relative to peers across time or geography. By anchoring theory in a tangible moment and two complementary visuals, the author ensures the subsequent framework will be read as an explanation of something seen, not a speculation about something imagined.

The chapter then names its central concept as a mechanism with inputs, outputs, and failure modes rather than as a slogan. In Introduction that mechanism is unpacked step by step: what conditions activate it, what observable signals indicate it is present, and what costs accrue when it is misapplied. A conceptual diagram organizes the idea, often as a matrix, flowchart, or causal loop with arrows that show how variables reinforce or dampen each other. A companion empirical chart plots historical realizations, such as dispersion of returns, frequency of errors, or duration of advantage, so the framework can be confronted with data. The exposition states boundary conditions and common misreadings, distinguishing contexts where the tool clarifies from those where it misleads, preparing the reader for the contrasting case.

The narrative then turns to a counterpoint that tests the same lens on unfamiliar material. This second anecdote in Introduction introduces a new protagonist or a later chapter in the original journey, complete with dated correspondence and the constraints that made the choice difficult at the time. A comparative visual organizes the contrast — for example diverging equity curves or a before-cost versus after-cost performance chart.
